        What I recommend
        Test one neural semantic parser followed by a deterministic, compositional compiler on checked reference meanings. The cached AMR already contains some relationships missing from the SRL-derived draft. A source-conditioned neural confidence model and a distribution over alternative logical forms are plausible additions, but neither repairs an absent or mistranslated meaning by itself. The comparison and limitations are below.
        1. Write reference meanings for a small, varied claim set. Goal: settle roles, source scope, alternatives and time independently of whether a program runs.
        2. Test one fixed neural semantic-parser frontend with compositional logical conversion. Goal: reuse the semantic relationships already present in AMR, while measuring its scope and source-alignment errors. Use the same frontend for the whole comparison.
        3. Measure candidate coverage and source-conditioned confidence. Goal: learn whether a small neural ranker can distinguish faithful candidates. Add probabilities over alternative logical forms only after checking candidate meanings and calibration; training on media remains deferred.
        Original parse → edits → compiled result
        Read the original failed or unfinished structure first, then each named attempt. The selector also preserves earlier typed-edit conditions. ARG0, ARG1 and related labels are SRL argument labels; their interpretation depends on the predicate. The separate meaning review checks the whole program, not only the edited fields.

        Probabilities over alternative logical forms
        A probabilistic parser can keep more than one interpretation and assign one categorical choice over them. This differs from making the claim the logical OR of every possible interpretation. The parser’s confidence should depend on the sentence; selecting whichever interpretation matches the media risks changing the claim.
        Alice saw Bob with a telescope.
        Reading 1: Alice used a telescope to see Bob. Reading 2: Bob had a telescope. In the constructed example, their parse weights are 0.6 and 0.4. Their supplied support probabilities are 0.9 and 0.1.
        Native DeepProbLog result: 0.6 × 0.9 + 0.4 × 0.1 = 0.58 support. OR over the two supplied observations gives 0.91, which asks a weaker question. These are stipulated values, not measured parser or media scores.
        For the second row, the parse weights are 0.54 and 0.36, with 0.10 reserved for no adequate parse. In the program, reading(P) selects interpretation P, uses(P,O) assigns its observation O, and answer(Y) returns outcome Y.
        Table 221. Constructed native inference. Parser abstention is distinct from insufficient evidence for a successfully parsed claim. No parser weights were learned or calibrated.

        Two alternative logical forms0.5800.4200.0000.000
        Retain probability of no adequate parse0.5220.3780.0000.100
        The backend implementation reuses a shared observation once. It also supports the case where no parse is available. A real system would need a source-conditioned model for the parse weights and checked candidate coverage; grammar validity or token likelihood is not a calibrated probability of faithful meaning.

        More general approaches and proposed next experiments
        Seventeen primary works were verified, and eleven candidate approaches are recorded. This is a local assessment. The external review did not run: automatic approval rejected sending unpublished project material to the external judge.
        Table 222. Proposals, not implemented replacements or new measured coverage gains.
        ApproachWhat it could solveWhat remains necessary
        One frozen semantic parser + compositional compilerRecover semantic links and explicit scope without retraining SRLChecked source meanings, source-span alignment and supported scope conversion
        Small source-conditioned neural rankerChoose faithful candidates using sentence and graph featuresNew checked positive/negative meanings; video-disjoint evaluation; a faithful candidate must exist
        Probability distribution over logical formsRepresent ambiguity and avoid committing to one unsupported readingCalibrated source-only weights, an explicit no-adequate-parse outcome and shared evidence variables
        Typed AST/grammar constraintsPrevent malformed roles, literals, declarations and scope structureSeparate evaluation of faithful meaning; well-typed programs can still be wrong
        A concrete neural version would score the sentence and each candidate logical form together with a small text encoder, such as a BERT-like cross-encoder. A cross-encoder reads both inputs jointly. A classification head would produce a match score, then normalize scores over candidates plus a no-adequate-parse option. It needs checked meaning labels and video-disjoint calibration; the current frozen Qwen check is not that learned model. The paper’s separate media relation classifiers would still use frozen visual/audio features.
        Relevant distinctions are established in PICARD, Synchromesh and ChopChop: they enforce checkable structure/properties, not an oracle for sentence meaning. Neural parser-ranker work and consistency-based semantic parsing address spurious programs; a correct verdict is not sufficient evidence for the right parse.
        Paper framing: uncertain language/environment interpretation already appears in P3, and recursive semantic parsing plus deterministic compilation appears in NL2Logic. The frontend alone is not our novelty. ADR-023 remains unchanged: the eventual verification contribution needs evidence on typed depiction/sound/speech/OCR support, media-conditioned binding models and shared evidence assignments.

        How the correction works
        1. Compile the original first. Only an actual direct failure can enter the correction path.
        2. Give the frozen model the original claim, dependency parse, SRL frames and failed logical form. The original wording controls meaning; parser labels can be wrong.
        3. Request at most eight JSON Patch operations. JSON Patch is a standard way to add, replace or remove fields. Each value must match the existing field type: a property needs a role and value, an argument needs a declared entity reference or typed literal, and a proposition needs a body and scope. The model cannot replace the entire formula or entity list.
        4. Validate, compile and return the actual errors. The feedback branch sees the exact field, missing content and relevant source links. The control sees a failure notice. Both allow at most two retries and stop at first automatic success. Correction: the saved generic retry messages did not explicitly retain the original error; the later structural comparison includes it in both branches.
        5. Inspect the whole completed program. Meaning review never triggers another model request. An inherited wrong role is still a failure, even when the requested field edit is correct.
        Generation uses frozen Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507, text only, greedy decoding, 1,536 output tokens and the same source-specific constraints in both branches. There are 605 unique model requests across the shared first attempt and two controls. No SRL model was retrained. Exact messages, raw edits, resulting structures, predicates and errors are in the inspector.

        Among the 218 no-draft failures, the direct compiler stops on 96 unattached clauses, 33 duplicate roles and 33 missing predicates; only ten are labelled missing SRL. A missing saved draft therefore often means the conversion aborted early, not that every parser supplied no useful information.
        Wrong relationships remain the main acceptance problem. “Robot on lane three…” gains three but also an unsupported relation from lane to Robot. “Sheinbaum: Movement promoted…” makes Sheinbaum the promoter rather than the source of the statement. “2025 Montreal map…” treats 2025 as the number of maps. The wind-speed claim still fails; the model moves adults into unrelated fields rather than completing the causal structure. Inspect these exact attempts.
        Hard checks also inherit parser mistakes: the dependency parse treats sweep as the subject of “Robot 1 sweep kicks Robot 2.” A subject-agreement check can reinforce that mistake. Field editing also cannot readily replace a wrong root or repair a major scope structure. More executable programs alone would hide these problems.

        1. Keep partial logical forms when direct parsing fails. Goal: make the 218 failures without a saved draft available for constrained correction, without inventing missing events.

Goal: allow repairs that field edits cannot express and measure whether additional executable programs actually preserve meaning.         Existing tools and methods
        Stanza supplies the relevant grammatical links, and AMR represents modifiers, shared nodes and conjunction/disjunction. Our cached examples already contain that information. AMR quantification is shallow; a correct graph does not remove the need for defined logical scope. A pretrained Stanza coreference module exists but was not benchmarked here.
        Logic-LM already uses symbolic translation and solver-error refinement. PICARD constrains formal syntax during decoding. These support trying the proposed alternatives; neither guarantees faithful compilation of these media claims.

        General changes tested
        • Remove duplicate auxiliary frames. When the parser supplies both “are” and “covered,” keep the lexical frame and retain the tense information. Genuine copulas such as “is gray” remain. This alone raises direct automatic passes to 1,960.
        • Keep attached adverbs. Previously omitted words such as “back,” “in” and “below” become conditions attached to their actual event or noun. They do not receive word-ignore credit. Scope-sensitive words such as “likely,” “presumably,” “only” and “all” are excluded from this repair. The final condition reaches 1,978 direct passes.
        • Resolve explicit interval references. “During this time” can inherit a unique stated parent interval on the same compiled event. A missing event still causes refusal. An omitted end date is resolved only within a same-day range; no midnight rollover is guessed. Whole-phrase SRL arguments are replaced when a phrase relation supplies their explicit object.
        • Test nominal events separately. “The collapse of a bridge blocks a road” can use one event variable for collapse and the subject of blocks. But lexical typing mistakes camera shots and electoral ridings for actions. Nominal typing stays off by default; these diagnostics are excluded from the corpus gains.
        These are conventional parsing repairs. NomBank explicitly annotates nominal predicates and their arguments; our WordNet/context heuristic is not a trained nominal semantic-role parser or a general word-sense disambiguator.

        Training interface: real features, native DeepProbLog
        A 270,595-parameter network uses 4,096-dimensional frozen Qwen3-VL features conditioned on the video frames and proposition. Its layers are LayerNorm, a 64-unit linear layer, GELU, a 3-output linear layer and softmax. The inputs are media/proposition representations, not three answer probabilities. Only the small network is updated.
        On four assistant-inspected color examples from one development clip, 30 native DeepProbLog epochs take 0.52 seconds on CPU after loading/compilation. Mean claim-level negative log likelihood falls from 1.2225 to 0.000511. Gradients reach the classifier; cached features and the old label-eligibility file remain unchanged.
        This is an engineering check that deliberately fits four examples, not a training result for the paper. Entity identities, school-bus descriptions, candidate coverage and time conditions are stipulated. There are no held-out videos, no learned evidence alignment and no audio labels. The original examples remain ineligible for empirical training. Full-corpus media feature extraction and binding evaluation have not begun.

          What changed, and why it is general
          • One value normalizer across argument positions: calendar dates, date–time pairs, durations and supported measurements use the same handling. Repeated time arguments keep their types. “Flight 2025” stays an identifier; a video time code is not silently converted into a clock.
          • Phrase-level relations: supported motion phrases such as “relative to” and “with respect to” bind a reference object. Supported spatial phrases bind a location. The governing predicate and dependency links constrain the interpretation. This is a bounded phrase inventory, not a complete preposition disambiguator.
          • Source alignments: each normalized value/relation records the original character span that produced it. A span receives credit only if its typed value or bound relation survives compilation. This supplements the word check; it does not prove correct meaning.
          • Semantic checks: an explicit time buried in an opaque phrase, or “During this time” without an interval reference, requests review. Copied quotations and typed raw times are handled separately.

          What was implemented
          • Multiple adjuncts on one event: “drive along a dock towards the ship” keeps both directions on the same driving event. Duplicate core participants are still checked.
          • Measurements: preserve values, both range bounds and units; distinguish four robots from a 100 m dash, and scalar magnitude 7.7 from an object count.
          • Absence: “no narration” means no matching narration/event exists. It does not introduce positive narration. Incomplete audio candidates give insufficient evidence.
          • Participant and source alignment: use explicit participant IDs; distinguish a clip depicting an event from a camera broadcasting a livestream as its object.
          These are opt-in compiler extensions. The historical default compiler reproduces all 2,375 saved outputs exactly. All 360 regression and extension tests pass. Some direct automatic passes still have incorrect meaning; those 16 are excluded from the 27 additions.
          Examples that explain the bottleneck
          • Two trucks: one event, two directions; direct repair, no model.
          • No narration: quantified absence, with no positive narration.
          • Boat capsizing: the event stays inside the clip’s depiction.
          • People covered in dust: even this short unchanged sentence lacks an attached semantic-role frame.
          • Robot 1/Robot 2: the split still fails participant alignment; explicit-ID support does not fix every parser analysis.
          • No containers fully in the water: the model adds “There are no containers,” which loses the restriction. This proposal also stops at composition.
          • Court/panel: both sentences compile, but the judges are attached to a disconnected panel.

          Why 449 claims still fail
          Current compilation coverage: 1,926/2,375 (81.09%), including two reviewed automatic splits. The direct compiler alone passes 1,924 (81.01%). These are content-check counts, not semantic accuracy.
          We have not shown that rewriting fails on the whole 19%. Only 31 original failures received the fixed rewrite experiment: 2 recovered and 29 remained. The other 420 remaining failures have not been rewritten. That deliberately selected sample cannot estimate how many of the 420 are recoverable.
          Table 237. First failing checks for all 449 remaining claims. A claim can have additional problems beyond its first rejection.
          First failing checkClaimsWhat it means
          Parser or compiler cannot form all required predicates227 (50.6%)Unlinked clauses, repeated roles, missing event frames, fragments or clauses left inside strings.
          Generated structure omits source content173 (38.5%)A candidate exists, but words or relationships from the original claim are missing.
          Unsupported operators or value types43 (9.6%)Absence, modality, alternatives, thresholds, time or numerical values need a supported logical interpretation.
          Explicit reference or media-context checks6 (1.3%)Source mentions, implicit subjects or media-description attachments cannot be aligned safely.
          179 failures already have a flagged program; 270 have no program. The earlier review of those same 179 candidates found 166 apparent content/structure gaps, 5 likely overstrict word alerts and 8 uncertain readings. These were local assistant judgments, not whole-claim correctness labels. Of the 179, 56 involved numbers/dates/units and 34 involved arguments/lists/noun phrases.
          Why simpler sentences still fail
          • The compiler can reject simple, meaningful sentences. “Two trucks drive along a dock towards the ship” gives two direction arguments. The current conversion permits only one distinct entity-valued argument per role, so repeated ARGM-DIR is rejected. Rewording may change the parser output, but the underlying limitation is the compiler interface.
          • Splitting does not add missing logical meaning. “The video has no audio” requires absence over possible audio events. A positive audio entity followed by a negated event is not equivalent. A speed such as 20–25 km/h also needs a value, range and unit, rather than a count of objects.
          • The subclaims must still share participants and context. “Robot 1” and “Robot 2” have the same noun head; our conservative aligner currently refuses that ambiguity instead of using the explicit IDs. The second-shot vehicle example has useful short sentences, but the adapter requires a simple source sentence to recover the depicted context.
          • The model sometimes changes the claim. It turns no narration into positive and negative narration; building housing a publisher into a building being constructed; or a sign quotation into world assertions. Successful JSON output and short clauses do not establish faithfulness.
          What the 31-case experiment actually found
          Of 29 unrecovered cases, 12 stop at component compilation, 10 at entity alignment, 3 at source-context alignment and 2 at conflicting descriptions. Two additional generated programs are rejected on review. These are pipeline stages, not independent root causes: an unfaithful split may already fail an earlier check.
          The model cannot solve missing compiler semantics just by simplifying syntax. Conversely, our conservative alignment can reject useful simplifications. The current results therefore mix model errors, compiler limitations and overly strict matching; they do not prove that all 449 claims are intrinsically difficult.

          3. Then test a stratified sample of the 420 untested failures once—measure where rewriting helps before finalizing it, rather than repeatedly tuning on the same 31 cases.

            When to stop compiler optimization
            My recommendation is to freeze the current grammar rules as the comparison baseline now. Keep correcting basic source-alignment, quotation-protection and validation bugs, but stop adding an open-ended rule for each new sentence shape. The last batch recovered 58 checks, so we have not measured a diminishing-return curve. The reason to move on is the paper goal and the mix of remaining structural problems, not a claim that the compiler is complete.
            Rewriting can simplify a sentence while retaining its information. It cannot safely invent a missing subject, resolve an ambiguous antecedent from world knowledge, change a quote, drop a modal or make unsupported quantified absence valid. In particular, no audio/no narration requires correct existence-and-negation scope; replacing it with a positive audio entity plus absent is not an established solution.
            Proposed rewrite pilot—before new DeepProbLog experiments
            1. Keep the compiler fixed. Compare original claims with minimally rewritten claims under the same predicates and checks.
            2. Use 40 development cases: 24 failed targets, eight unchanged controls and eight ambiguity/unsupported-semantic guards. Select targets with a reviewed missing value or relationship; exclude overstrict-only alerts from semantic-recovery counts. Use one frozen text model on the claim and existing text parses; exclude truth labels and media observations. Allow an unchanged result or explicit refusal. Reserve source groups before prompt tuning.
            3. Review original → rewrite → predicates. Check who did what to whom, shared participants, quantities with their owners, dates, tense/aspect, polarity, modality, exact quotations and source scope. Repeating a sentence into several clauses must not lose shared identity.
            4. Use proposed development gates: at least 12 of 24 failed targets become reviewed faithful compiled outputs; no unchanged-control regressions; zero accepted critical information changes. An increased syntax-pass count alone is insufficient.
            5. Then freeze the complete preparation pipeline. Proceed to relation learning and DeepProbLog inference/training on checked compiled examples, retaining refusals. The 1,924 automatic passes are not a clean training set.
            These are proposed gates, not results or a statistical accuracy guarantee. At the time of this audit the rewrite layer was unimplemented. The subsequent pilot has its own results tab. This audit is development context, not held-out rewrite evidence.

            Failure patterns
            • Diagnostic text encourages repairs but can also prompt invented signers, mission context and comparative references.
            • The model sometimes claims a rewrite while emitting the exact original; its explanations are not evidence of successful repair.
            • Reparsing can recover a missing participant while assigning another role incorrectly, such as sweep as the kicking actor or track as a running actor.
            • Word coverage misses typed-quantity errors: a rate interval can become object-count bounds, and a fractional orbit count can remain exactly three.
            • Equivalent English negation does not repair the compiler's unsupported quantified-absence scope.
            • Exact names and quotations still change despite explicit instructions; surface checks and review reject those proposals.
            Next steps and intended goals
            1. Review the three retained diagnostic-prompt recoveries and rejected examples with the user—confirm the assistant fidelity judgments before treating them as training structures.
            2. Keep the compiler and both prompts frozen; address only the identified quantity/scope contracts or test a stronger rewriter in a separate fixed comparison—avoid another open-ended series of grammar rules.
            3. Repeat a bounded fidelity evaluation before any corpus-wide rewrite; prepare DeepProbLog training only from checked structures after that gate.
            Original words, cached parses, old compiler outputs and historical source archives are preserved. The 40 comparisons and judgments are all available below; no accepted-count increase is presented as a media-verification result.

            Split a claim into simpler, linked sentences
            The user intended sentence-structure simplification: turn one difficult claim into short subclaims, compile each, then preserve how they relate. The earlier one-sentence restriction excluded this approach. Its negative results do not establish that sentence splitting is unhelpful.
            This is the established NLP task split-and-rephrase. Discourse-aware simplification also retains context links between sentences; LLM split-and-rephrase research reports remaining splitting-compliance limitations. Here splitting is a preparation component, not a new task or the paper’s main contribution.
            What the two experiments establish
            Automatic: one frozen Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 request for each of 31 previously inspected direct failures, with one fixed prompt. No passing-control call, media, truth label, training or per-claim prompt selection. The prompt uses a distinct Alice/photo example.
            Assistant-written diagnostic: eight selected cases after inspecting Qwen’s proposals. Seven receive clean splits and one no-audio case is explicitly declined. This isolates whether the compiler/composition can work when the proposed structure is clean. It is not a measured gain of the automatic splitter, an independent test or human gold.

            What changed in the implementation
            The underlying38 compiler files are unchanged. A separate adapter renames clause-local IDs, applies explicit shared mentions, and reuses existing conjunction, relative, source-content and temporal operators. It extends an existing depiction context instead of projecting its child into the world. Attributes inherit their containing evidence route. Conflicting descriptions are refused rather than silently moved across contexts. Fifteen composition tests and17 rewrite/routing tests pass.
            The initial source freeze and outputs are retained. After proposal inspection, diagnostic parsing was extended to invalid-link cases so component quality can be measured separately; capitalization is allowed in mention alignment; source predicates are checked; the adapter was corrected to reuse pre-existing depiction contexts and the existing route-inheritance function. No new sentence-pattern rule is added to the direct compiler. All cases remain development data.
